title: Sudden pile-up caught on camera
description:
Report summary details:
ICR: 21503306 
Date/Time: 04/14/2021 04:45
District: 2500 West Metro 
Location: Southbound Highway 169 at I-694 , Brooklyn Park, Hennepin County
 
Summary: Vehicles on southbound 169 had lost control on an icy bridge deck. One of the vehicle occupants had exited their vehicle and was contacted by an incoming Honda Odyssey. The individual involved was transported.
 
Road Condition: Snow/Ice
 
Outside agencies: 
Hennepin County Deputies, 
Brooklyn Park Police, 
North Ambulance

Last updated: 04/29/2021 10:09

transcript.text: This seemingly peaceful early morning view is about to be interrupted, because in only a moment, a 10-car pile-up is going to happen. The roadways are wet, but the bridge deck is icy, and on the far side of the bridge, there's a crash blocking both lanes. One final element in play is the fact that the gentle arch of the bridge is limiting the visibility of oncoming traffic to see what awaits them on the far side. The sudden change in traction, combined with a hard-to-see crash, blocking both lanes, creates a ripe environment for a pile-up. But if you're in the middle of a pile-up, what should you do? Any answer may involve trade-offs. One car opted to drive upstream to help get out of the way, and moments later, a vehicle careened into the spot they had occupied only seconds earlier. The car that went against traffic happened to position their vehicle, intended to be able to intentionally or not, at the apex of the bridge, which may have helped get the attention of other drivers and help them to perk up to the situation unfolding in front of them. In this video, one individual exited his vehicle, stayed on the shoulder, but did not get over the guardrail. Moments later, a minivan slid into him, unfortunately. Other individuals who exited and used a guardrail or concrete wall to separate them from traffic were not injured. The DOT Plow arrived less than a minute into the event, and its high-profile lighting likely helped in the pile-up by providing sufficient warning to incoming drivers. In this video, we looked primarily at environmental factors contributing to pile-ups, and initial observations suggest a sudden change in traction, a blocking crash, and limited visibility, in this case, the rise of a bridge, all created a risky environment for a multi-vehicle crash. In future videos, we'll take a closer look at driver behavior.
